players.product: gas & liquid delivery subsystems for etch/deposition tools (Lam, Applied)

quarterly_data.signal: Q4 2025 results (non-GAAP): revenue of $223.6 million came in above the midpoint of guidance but modestly down from Q3; management believes Q4 represents the trough period of this cycle, with the recent softening in certain end markets and applications already showing signs of recovery. Gross margin of 11.7% was 70 basis points above the midpoint of guidance on modestly better execution against lower volumes and unfavorable product mix; operating expenses $23.4 million; operating income $2.7 million; EPS of $0.01 at the upper end of expectations. Cash and equivalents $98.3 million (a $6 million increase from Q3); free cash flow $6 million after $3 million of capital expenditures; DSOs 29 days; inventory turns 3.3; year-end total debt $123 million (down from $129 million a year ago); net debt coverage ratio 1.7.
quarterly_data.figure: revenue $223.6 million; gross margin 11.7%; operating income $2.7 million; EPS $0.01; cash $98.3 million; total debt $123 million

quarterly_data.signal: Q1 2026 guidance: revenue of $240 million to $260 million, which at the midpoint equates to double-digit growth from the Q4 trough; the outlook has strengthened since the January webcast, with every weekly customer forecast update showing strengthening demand. Gross margin 12% to 13%; Q1 operating expenses approximately $24 million (seasonal payroll adjustments, audit fees and variable compensation); EPS $0.08 to $0.16 on 35.1 million diluted shares. 2026 model: a relatively consistent OpEx run rate of $24 million supports the revenue ramp (a full-year increase of about 5% vs fiscal 2025); net interest expense approximately $7 million for 2026; non-GAAP effective tax rate 20% to 25%, higher because of the geographic distribution of profits and the sunsetting of Ichor's Singapore pioneer status in early 2026.
quarterly_data.figure: Q1 revenue $240 million to $260 million; gross margin 12% to 13%; EPS $0.08 to $0.16; 2026 OpEx run rate $24 million; tax rate 20% to 25%

quarterly_data.signal: 2026 demand outlook: customer demand in Ichor's primary served markets has continued to strengthen since November and the January webcast; Ichor says it is now operating in a sustained demand ramp driven by fundamental technology transitions and strategic capacity additions - increased adoption of gate-all-around architectures, accelerating growth in high bandwidth memory, and rising capital intensity in advanced logic and advanced packaging - which increase etch and deposition intensity, the segment where Ichor is most highly levered. Management sees every quarter of 2026 as a growth quarter (revenue still second-half weighted, with additional demand pulling forward into the first half that the CEO would not call pull ahead) and expects growth in nearly every application with nearly every customer; it gave no full-year guide, but the CEO said an analyst's WFE growth range of around 15% to 20% is where Ichor is coalescing as well and that Ichor is well set up to be in that range, if not outperform. Visibility: the six-month window is very solid, customers' second-half (Q3/Q4) slotting is very solid compared with a normal year, and Ichor's view of 2027 is very similar to what its customers say; on the current 2027 trajectory the CEO thinks Ichor can get back to some historical revenue levels.

Growth mix and end markets: the vast majority of Q1's sequential growth comes from deposition and etch (the transcript prints 'Depenet'), with a slight increase in the non-semiconductor business; every segment of the market is growing, which the CEO said is why many are calling this a super cycle. AI applications are the driver in memory - there is a lack of capacity in DRAM and NAND driving much of the demand profile Ichor sees - and foundry and logic are also strong this year. Fiscal 2025 growth came primarily from etch and deposition, partially offset by softening EUV build rates and decreased demand in certain trailing-edge markets. EUV is roughly flat quarter over quarter and expected to pick up late in 2026: the lithography customer still has inventory to digest, which Ichor expects to be digested by roughly Q3 with some uptick in Q4 (with some unknowns), and that customer expects growth in the second half of 2026 into 2027. Ichor's revenue forecast is starting to match what its two biggest customers are saying, which management reads as a good indication that inventory levels are coming down, need to be replenished and have really burnt through from the last cycle; gas panels, the bulk of Ichor's business, carry little inventory, unlike the non-configurable EUV system.

Gross margin path: beginning Q2, gross profit dollars are expected to grow around twice the rate of revenues as the year progresses, with the global footprint realignment driving meaningful margin improvement by midyear and structurally eliminating the primary sources of the margin challenges faced in 2025. The first half is heavy in gas panels and carries transient headwinds from moving machining capacity between facilities (in place before exiting the first half, temporarily reducing internal supply) and from turning on the Malaysia facility (baked into the Q1 guide); second-half margin growth comes from incremental volume leverage as the redeployed tools come online, a stronger machining and components mix, and flow-through from the non-semi business. Asked by an analyst whether the 15% second-half gross margin target (the crosswalk he cited from Ichor's slides published last month) still holds, with incremental progress in Q2 and a pickup in the second half, the CEO said that is how he would model it; he declined to put a timeline on the 18% to 20% gross margin level an analyst cited as previous targets but expects significant earnings leverage moving through 2027 as components kick in.

Global footprint realignment: Ichor has been expanding its Mexico machining capacity (expansion complete later in 2026) and building a new manufacturing center in Malaysia, the largest facility in Ichor's history, which began operation last month; these will be the high-volume manufacturing centers for Ichor-branded products and give the capacity needed for the demand ramp. Relocating a portion of machining assets to these sites temporarily reduces capacity for those components but will not gate Ichor's ability to support customer demand. The Malaysia facility is two miles from Ichor's current second-largest facility, which builds essentially every weldment; it adds machining and components capacity for a ramp expected to continue through 2026 into 2027, with headwinds baked into Q1 and tailwinds seen in 2027. The CEO sees little to no risk in Mexico, which already runs pretty high volumes, and a little higher qualification risk in Malaysia. Capex was close to 4% of revenue in 2025, much of it for the Malaysia facility, and will moderate to around 3% of revenue in 2026 (equipment deployment in Malaysia and rebalancing machining equipment within North America). Restructuring charges were about $10 million in Q4; the majority of the effort is complete, with some further activity as the US facilities being realigned wind down.
quarterly_data.figure: 2026 capex around 3% of revenue (2025 close to 4%); Q4 restructuring about $10 million

quarterly_data.signal: Diversification and share gains: Ichor's commercial space business grew significantly in 2025 and, while still a small portion of revenue, has grown to the point where Ichor's fifth largest customer is now outside the semiconductor industry; recent commercial-space design wins are beginning to translate into meaningful revenue growth that could outpace semiconductor growth in 2026. That customer is a sub 5% customer today with margins accretive to Ichor's profile, and the medium-term goal is to make it a 10% customer (harder to reach given the semi ramp). The CEO wants to win share during this ramp cycle first in commercial space / non-semi machining, then across all of Ichor's componentry and in gas panels, and to become more balanced across the platforms Ichor is on, since customers divvy out share by platform.
quarterly_data.figure: commercial space customer sub 5% today; medium-term goal 10% customer
